title: Indiscernible sequences
summary: Turn finite Ramsey homogeneity into a new indiscernible sequence over parameters, preserving source patterns and the original structure by compactness.
abstract: An increasing list of rational numbers has a uniform pattern: every increasing finite selection answers the same parameter-free order questions. Indiscernibility asks for this agreement for every first-order formula, including formulas with fixed parameters. Ramsey’s theorem can make finitely many tests uniform on an infinite subsequence, but even a countable family of predicates can prevent any original subsequence from satisfying every test. Compactness instead constructs a new sequence in an elementary extension, preserving all statements about the old structure. The new sequence can have any infinite linear order as its index set, while every finite pattern of its truth values already occurs in the source. Distinguishing order-indiscernibility, permutation-invariance and repeated tuple coordinates keeps the resulting uniformity precise.
